conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility / who must ventilate when cooking
stove access and timing (when the stove will be freed)
moving personal laundry / risk of getting clothes wet
establishing a standing household rule about ventilation
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents give concrete practical reasons (A: cooking time; C: laundry will get wet), which grounds positions in observable consequences.
There is some repeated restatement of requests (D repeatedly asking for the rack/window; A repeatedly stating they won't leave the stove).
Public environment updates reliably reflect actions (extractor on, rack moved), keeping the dialogue grounded.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent C moved the drying rack (practical obstacle to opening the rain-facing window removed), which partially settled the laundry-related obstruction. However, Agent A still occupies the stove for several more minutes and no agreement was reached on a standing rule or on future ventilation responsibilities, so substantive conflicts about stove access and normative responsibility remain.
position_change_notes: Agent C changed position by moving the drying rack in Round 6 (evidence: 'I've moved the drying rack to a sheltered spot'), conceding the practical obstacle.

Agent A consistently retained their position of not leaving the stove during cooking and conditioned window opening on the rack being moved ('If someone moves the laundry, I'll open it'); no substantive change from A by the transcript end.

Agent B maintained focus on ventilation responsibility and requested a future promise, but accepted the immediate extractor use; Agent D remained ready to start and repeatedly requested updates, softening by waiting for the rack move rather than forcibly taking action.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A refuses to leave the stove and rejects a rule imposed during the incident; Agent B demands immediate ventilation and a standing rule that cooks must ventilate. Agent A turns on the extractor (complies with the immediate ventilation request) but explicitly refuses the imposed rule and to release the stove, so opposing substantive positions (who must ventilate; stove access) remain.

Agent A affirms the extractor is on and will keep cooking, offering to open the window only if someone moves the laundry; Agent B asks for a promise to switch the extractor on next time. The immediate practical request (use extractor now) is satisfied, reducing intensity, but the normative dispute over responsibility for ventilation and the stove-access demand remain unresolved.

Agent C refuses others moving the drying rack and offers to move it in five minutes (introducing a timing constraint); Agent D asks for three minutes instead. This introduces a distinct but related incompatibility (when/who moves the laundry) while prior issues (stove occupancy, ventilation responsibility) persist.

Agent A asserts ~10 minutes remaining and will not leave the stove, explicitly asking Agent C to move the rack in three minutes; Agent D repeats readiness and requests the rack moved now or to avoid using their prep space. Multiple incompatible demands (A's refusal to yield stove; D's urgency; C's unwillingness to have others move their rack) intensify the disagreement.

Agent A reiterates they will not step away and estimates eight minutes left; Agent D repeatedly asks for updates and requests Agent C move the rack. No substantive concessions or agreements occur; the core incompatibilities (stove timing, responsibility for moving laundry/ventilation) persist unchanged.

Agent C physically moves the drying rack to a sheltered spot (resolving the laundry/open-window obstacle). Agent D thanks C and asks Agent A to open the window; Agent A has not yet opened the window or released the stove, so stove-access timing and the broader rule about ventilation remain unresolved. Overall conflict intensity falls because the practical barrier is removed.

substantive_insights: The central tension is practical (avoiding wet laundry) versus responsibility for managing shared odour; these produce competing demands rather than a pure preference difference.
A immediate technical mitigation (extractor on) reduced urgency but did not resolve the normative dispute about who should bear ventilation duties.
A concrete action (C moving the rack) converted a conditional promise into a resolvable practical state, demonstrating how factual concessions can partially resolve multi-issue conflicts.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 6 because the final status is partially_resolved.
